problem_statement: adminmart/MatDash-Nextjs-Free (rebranded here as Cindershift, an on-call operations console for engineering teams) is a Next.js 16 App Router + Tailwind v4 admin console. Every console route renders inside a persistent sidebar + header DashboardLayout. Two changes are in scope. (1) A shared 'Operations pulse' rail must greet the responder at the top of EVERY core console route - the home dashboard (/), the Revenue & inventory table (/utilities/table), and the responder profile (/user-profile) - as an on-brand MatDash white card carrying a per-route context line, four pulse tiles (Active incidents, Pages sent, Services healthy, Mean ack time), and a monitoring-window toggle (Live / 24h) whose readout must update live when the window is clicked. (2) The home dashboard also carries a 'Product priority board' strip of four metric tiles (Open priorities, Shipping this week, Blocked items, Avg cycle time); on a 390px phone the board's tile row is pinned to a fixed 720px non-wrapping width, so it is far wider than the viewport and drags the whole document into horizontal overflow. Implement the Operations pulse rail consistently across all three routes in the MatDash card language, wire the Live/24h window toggle so the readout reflects the selected window, and repair the priority-board strip so it reflows to fit 390px mobile with no horizontal overflow - all while keeping copy, card content, and the rest of the MatDash console shell unchanged, and the app rendering fully offline with no console or network errors.
required_content: The 'Operations pulse' rail is present on all three console routes (home, /utilities/table, /user-profile) as an on-brand MatDash white card headed 'Operations pulse', carrying its per-route context line and the four pulse tiles (Active incidents, Pages sent, Services healthy, Mean ack time).

The rail's monitoring-window toggle updates its readout live: after clicking the 24h window on the home dashboard, the readout reads 'Window: 24h rollup' (it reads 'Window: Live snapshot' before the click).

The 'Product priority board' strip renders the same four tiles (Open priorities, Shipping this week, Blocked items, Avg cycle time) with identical text and values on every viewport, and on a 390px mobile viewport the dashboard home has no horizontal overflow beyond a small tolerance.
On desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) the priority board and Operations pulse rail lay out cleanly with no horizontal overflow and no visual regression from the MatDash card palette.

The sidebar, top bar, header, Revenue Forecast, New Customers, Total Income, Revenue by Product table, Daily activities timeline, and blog cards remain present and unchanged in content and structure; no new console errors or failed network requests are introduced.
design_constraints: Preserve the MatDash console design language: card grid, rounded white card surfaces, primary/secondary/success/error accent chips, the persistent sidebar + header shell, and the existing section order. The Operations pulse rail must read as a native MatDash white card, not an off-brand dark slab.
Mount the Operations pulse rail from the shared DashboardLayout so it appears consistently on all three console routes; do not add it to only the route you happen to edit.
The window toggle must actually update the readout on click (not merely move the active-button highlight); the post-click readout must reflect the selected window.

Repair the priority board by letting its tile row reflow to fit narrow viewports; do not mask the overflow by clipping the row or hiding overflow at the body/html level. The repair must fit 390px mobile, 834px tablet, and 1440px desktop.
Keep the Next.js build pipeline intact - `next build` must still emit a working console and `next start` must serve the home, table, and profile routes.
state_constraints: desktop_home / mobile_home / tablet_home capture the dashboard home at 1440/390/834px; the Operations pulse rail and priority board fit with no horizontal overflow after the change.

mobile_home and mobile_board capture the 390px home scrolled to the priority board; with the defect the board's tile row forces the document ~398px wider than the viewport, and the repair brings horizontal overflow within tolerance.
desktop_pulse and mobile_pulse capture the home Operations pulse rail in view; the rail must stay in the MatDash white-card palette (not an off-brand dark slab) and reflow tidily on mobile.
desktop_table_rail and desktop_profile_rail capture the Operations pulse rail on /utilities/table and /user-profile; the rail must be present and consistent on both secondary routes.
desktop_window_24h captures the home rail after clicking the 24h window toggle; the readout must read 'Window: 24h rollup' (changed from 'Window: Live snapshot').
desktop_revenue, desktop_activity, and mobile_activity confirm the Revenue by Product table, Daily activities timeline, and mobile document are unchanged and overflow-free after the change.

change_completion: The Operations pulse rail is present and consistent across all three console routes with its window toggle wired to update the readout live.
Clicking the 24h window on the home rail updates the readout to 'Window: 24h rollup'.
The mobile dashboard home no longer overflows horizontally: the priority-board strip reflows to fit a 390px viewport.
design_consistency: The Operations pulse rail and priority board preserve the MatDash console identity, white card surfaces, and accent-chip palette across every route.
The rail is mounted uniformly from the shared layout (present on all three routes), not added ad hoc to a single page, and is not restyled into an off-brand dark card.
responsive: At 390px the priority-board row wraps or flexes down so the document width stays within the viewport, and the Operations pulse rail reflows tidily.
At 834px and 1440px the board and rail lay out cleanly with no horizontal overflow.
regression: Sidebar, top bar, header, Revenue Forecast, New Customers, Total Income, Revenue by Product, Daily activities, and blog cards remain present and unchanged.
No new console errors or failed network requests appear on any captured state.

author_notes: Repo-grounded design_continuity + repair task on the MatDash Next.js 16 App Router admin console (rebranded Cindershift). L4 with four orthogonal design gates: D6 no_horizontal_overflow (the 'Product priority board' fixed-720px tile row overflows a 390px phone; reference wraps, baseline 398px, bad 198px), D3 visual_regression (the shared 'Operations pulse' rail must stay in the MatDash white/#5d87ff card palette; bad recolours it to a dark navy slab), D2 dom_assertions cross-page (the rail must be present on home + /utilities/table + /user-profile; baseline mounts it home-only, bad home+table only), and D4 interaction_assertions (clicking the 24h window toggle must update the readout to 'Window: 24h rollup'; bad's stale-closure handler leaves it 'Window: Live snapshot'). The baseline fails D6+D3+D2 but passes D4 (its home rail has the correct live handler), and the bad fails all four. Content and shell copy are held identical across legs. Offline INFRA identical across all legs: @iconify/react runtime icon fetch replaced by a local inline-icon shim, next/font/google Manrope replaced by a local font stack, and the rail container clips its own horizontal box so only the priority board drives document overflow.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: MatDash-Nextjs-Free is a runnable Next.js 16 App Router + Tailwind v4 admin console (rebranded Cindershift) whose persistent sidebar + header DashboardLayout wraps every route, making it an ideal host for an L4 design-continuity task: a shared Operations pulse rail across three console routes (cross-page consistency, visual fidelity, interactive window toggle) plus a fixed-width priority board carrying a mobile horizontal-overflow repair.
